newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SEEN SHORT BUT RATES STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SEEN SHORT BUT RATES STABLE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted little changed on Thursday despite a forecast shortage of cash in the system, dealers said.
The market opened with a Z$96.2 millon surplus but the central bank forecast it would close short of Z$194 million, for which reason it was not auctioning any treasury bills.
However the central bank paper was being traded on the secondary market at 24.80 percent, unchanged from Wednesday, while call money ranged between 24 and 26 percent from around 24 percent.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.75 percent and sold at 26 percent while bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 25 percent on the selling side.
